newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU bans Belgian export aid, warns French textiles.
newsitem.headline: EU bans Belgian export aid, warns French textiles.

text.p: The European Commission ordered Belgium on Wednesday to recover 11.4 billion francs in salary- linked charges that exporting firms should have paid in 1995.
The Commission was ruling on a Belgian scheme called Maribel which allows exporters facing international competition to pay reduced social security contributions.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warned France that a scheme designed to help textile firms would meet the same fate.
"That too is not acceptable," he told Belgian radio RTBF. "There too we will take a decision," Van Miert said.

The Commission ruled that Maribel violated EU fair competition rules because of its "clear objective and effect of advantaging Belgium-established firms to the detriment of their foreign competitors".

Earlier this year the Commission said it had strong doubts about a proposed French plan to help its textile industry. Last year it asked Italy to scrap a similar scheme designed to support the shoe-making sector.

In all these cases, the Commission has made it crystal clear that it will not tolerate schemes designed to improve the competitive advantage of specific sectors as this distorted fair trade in the 15-nation bloc.

It has instead encouraged governments to provide general, across the board reductions in salary-linked contributions to the national health and pension schemes which are the highest in the developed world.
